sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- quote + venue] Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said on Saturday he was 'extremely worried' that a new escalation in the US-Iran war would be more destructive and have a major impact, speaking at the IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain. Quote: 'The second round will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere. We have to draw lessons from the past.' Reuters context: a June interim agreement failed to secure a lasting ceasefire or restore normal shipping through Hormuz.
sections.what_verified: 2 counted families: Reuters (T1) reporting the speech directly + Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) liveblog reporting the speech directly. Straits Times/Arab News/Dawn/JPost relays of Reuters add no family.
sections.what_disputed: Counterweight inside the same window: IRGC spokesman Akraminia (1300-06) warns the flames of war would engulf a wider area -- the region is hearing warnings from both a mediator-adjacent capital (Cairo) and Tehran's military in the same hour. No party disputes that Abdelatty said this.
sections.why_matters: Cairo breaks the Doha optimism: Egypt warns round two will be 'more dangerous, more destructive' -- the Arab warning against the breakthrough headline
sections.context: Background: IN-WINDOW (AJ liveblog 08:40 GMT = 12:40 ; Reuters 08:20 UTC) -- Egypt FM Badr Abdelatty at IISS Manama Dialogue: 'extremely worried' a second round in the US-Iran war 'will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere'
